clue.text: Decline storage facility in Orient

definitions.meaning: to decline is to sink or fall away, as a business might
in India and East Asia a warehouse is traditionally called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means sink or fall, and the single word is the Anglo-Indian term for a warehouse.

clue.text: Copy goes wrong without right stabilizing device

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters sit around the other one
wrong says the letters are set out incorrectly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Copying went badly without the correct balancing gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside: R goes inside the rearranged COPYGOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning wheel mounted on gimbals keeps orientation and is used to stabilize ships and aircraft.

clue.text: Fault in drain to sea shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to drain someone is to tire them
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A defect in a drain leading out to sea is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' turns TIREMED round to give the answer; 'in' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a mark against someone for a failing or shortcoming.

clue.text: Fatherless child making relatively large donation

definitions.meaning: read as a mite (small child) belonging to a widow, one whose father has died
in Mark's Gospel a poor widow's two small coins are worth more, in proportion, than rich men's gifts

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical small coin offering is large relative to the giver's means; read literally it is a bereaved mother's little one.

clue.text: A great admirer I deceive, in time

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating or swindling them
in time means eventually, that is later

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to deceiving a fan in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships an idol is, by extension, any devoted fan or admirer.

clue.text: Critical outbursts from supporter upset groups of people

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: an aid is a helper or supporter
tribes are groups of people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Angry rants come from a backer annoyed by factions.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, an outburst of criticism.

clue.text: Football hooligan, for example, is abroad supporting side

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supports another by sitting below it

parts.note: L for left is one side
someone abroad is out of the country, out

explanation.surface: A soccer thug overseas cheers on his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts OUT below L. 'Supporting side' looks like a fan backing a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A football hooligan is one example of a boorish, aggressive young man.

clue.text: Man promises to repay without any interest

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A man offers IOUs and pays no interest on the loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' suggests money on a loan; it is the opposite of boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull or boring holds no interest for anyone.

clue.text: Engineers organize broadcast again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to run an event is to organize it

explanation.surface: Technicians arrange for a repeat transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a programme a second time is to repeat it.

clue.text: Queen to take over without a conclusive vote

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are removed

parts.note: to annex a territory is to take it over
X is the mark placed on a ballot paper, and here it is the closing letter

explanation.surface: A monarch seizes power with no decisive ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was a queen of Great Britain, 1702 to 1714.

clue.text: Heads off tram — lad ran fast

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its head, meaning its first letter is chopped off

explanation.surface: A boy jumps off a tram and runs away quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' removes T, L and R from tram, lad and ran, leaving RAM, AD and AN. 'Fast' looks like an adverb for running; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim holy month is observed by fasting from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Rent was underpaid, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tenant complains the rent payment fell partly short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for housing, but here it is the past participle of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as the past participle of rend means torn apart, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Sort of blonde that's covered in cream in summer?

definitions.meaning: a reddish-golden hair colour is described with this fruit's name

definitions.text: that's covered in cream in summer?
definitions.meaning: a summer fruit traditionally served with cream, as at Wimbledon

explanation.definitionFit: The fruit names a reddish-blonde hair shade and is the classic British summer dessert with cream.

clue.text: Little woman's at home to knit

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women; the 's is a link
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A small lady stays home doing her knitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knit' is not about wool here: it means unite, as broken bones knit together.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to bring together or unite, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Still with nothing to debate?

definitions.meaning: read as a meeting lacking a motion, a proposal put up for debate

explanation.definitionFit: Being stationary means not moving; read in two parts it is lacking a debating proposal.

clue.text: Leader leaves the floor, taking a new type of seat

indicators.note: the leading letter departs, so the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: the bottom of something is its floor or base

explanation.surface: A chairman stands up from the floor and takes a fresh kind of chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low upholstered seat or footstool without a back.

clue.text: The flower of Greek youth

definitions.meaning: the daffodil genus of spring flowers
in Greek myth a beautiful young man fell in love with his own reflection

explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil genus is named after the mythical vain youth who became the flower.

clue.text: May, for example, flourish

definitions.meaning: may is the hawthorn's flowering, an example of a tree's flowers
to flourish is to thrive or develop well

explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn flowers, called may, are an instance of tree flowers, and to thrive is to bloom figuratively.

clue.text: Alter song, maybe, for 27

indicators.note: alter says the following letters are changed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Changing a song, perhaps, for a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the rich man of 27 across. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a very wealthy person, matching the proverbial rich man.

clue.text: The line that can be twisted into a torque

indicators.note: twisted says the letters are wrung into a new order, fitting the torque image

explanation.surface: A line that might be bent into a turning force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' and 'into' are links. Torque is the physics term for a twisting force, so 'twisted' blends into the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary line round the Earth's middle is often called simply the Line by sailors.

clue.text: Open in university show

parts.note: being up means in residence at university, as at Oxford
a front is an outward show or pretence

explanation.surface: An exhibition opens at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank and honest is being candid and direct.

clue.text: Put saint in here

parts.note: in here means inside, which is within

explanation.surface: An instruction to place a holy figure inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link; the clue says to put S before WITHIN, and the whole clue points at the saint whose name results.
explanation.definitionFit: St Swithin is the English saint whose day, 15 July, is linked to forty days of rain.

clue.text: Composer, with hesitation, becomes a weapon holder

parts.note: Gustav Holst composed The Planets
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A musician hesitating turns into a gun case.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather case worn at the hip carries a pistol.

clue.text: Instrument provided with iron case

indicators.note: the iron's letters form a case wrapping around the other word

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
provided means on condition that, i.e. if

explanation.surface: A musical instrument comes supplied in a metal box.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small high-pitched flute played in military bands.

clue.text: Commander in endless bother is the centre of attention

indicators.note: in places the officer inside the trimmed word
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: fuss means bother or commotion
OC is Officer Commanding, a military commander

explanation.surface: An officer in an endless fuss draws all eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: OC (Officer Commanding) is the usual crossword commander; 'Commander' tempts CO, which puts the letters in the wrong order.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is a point on which attention is concentrated.

clue.text: Silly rhymes, whether desired or not

definitions.meaning: a jingling phrase made of two rhyming halves, which sounds silly
regardless of whether one wants it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rhyming reduplication meaning regardless of wishes.

clue.text: Foreign song lacked veracity

definitions.meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.definitionFit: The German word for song names a Romantic art song, and the English verb means fibbed.

clue.text: Ruler with tyrannous air, totally heartless

indicators.note: each word has all its inner letters removed, leaving only first and last letters

explanation.surface: An autocrat with a despotic manner, utterly without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'totally heartless' leaves TS and AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Sources can supply needs of rich man

indicators.note: can supply suggests the letters can be reworked to furnish a new word

explanation.surface: Funding sources can meet a wealthy man's requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs of' is a link: the rearranged letters supply what the rich man needs, his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus, king of Lydia, was proverbially wealthy, so a very rich person is called this.

clue.text: Choose artist's classic work

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist

explanation.surface: Pick an artist's masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles and an opera by Strauss, a classic work of art.

clue.text: He can make one's traits appear funny

definitions.text: He can make one's traits appear funny

indicators.note: appear funny says the letters are made to look odd, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is I and the possessive 's here gives S

explanation.surface: A comedian mocks people's characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' is a link. 'appear funny' rearranges I, S and TRAITS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of satire ridicules people's foibles to comic effect.

clue.text: Underworld boss loves flower-girl

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so loves is O's
Iris is both a flower and a girl's name

explanation.surface: A gangland chief adores a girl who sells flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster; it is the Egyptian god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god who ruled the realm of the dead.
